about: Synthetic scenarios for a first check. Each has a source and a destination CSV in its folder, the configuration the CSV check page uses (config.json, as the page writes it), and the result to expect with each set of premises. offline/bench/golden.py runs each expectation as a golden case named scenario-ID-PREMISES; ui/src/test/offline/scenarios.test.ts checks that each result is the one written here.

scenarios.title: Contacts synced to a CRM
scenarios.description: A contact list synced to a CRM: one phone number changed, and one contact is missing.

expect.why: C-1002 has a different phone number, and C-1003 is not in an export stated to cover the whole object.

The different phone number of C-1002 is a Mismatch on its own, because the row exists. C-1003 is not found, but without the destination statement that does not show it is missing, so it is Unverified.

scenarios.title: Orders compared with trim and casefold
scenarios.description: An order export compared with the rules casefold for the email and trim for the status: the files differ only in letter case and spaces.

expect.why: Only letter case and spaces differ, and the two rules ignore them.
No rule fails, but without the statements a record found once is not shown to be the only one with its key, and the batch is not known to be whole.

scenarios.title: An extra record in the destination
scenarios.description: A price list whose destination holds one record that is not in the source, checked with scope exact.

expect.why: SKU-399 is in the destination and not in a source stated to be the whole batch.
The extra row exists, so the destination statement is not needed for it. Without that statement the four source records are Unverified.
SKU-399 is listed without a conclusion: it could belong to a source record that is not in the file.

scenarios.title: A source row with an empty key
scenarios.description: A member list in which one source row has no key.

expect.why: A row without a key cannot be matched, so the source population is unknown even with the source statement.
The row without a key cannot be matched, and nothing else is established either.
